headline: GOLD DROPS BELOW $4,500, silver below $75 as Iran-Israel clash resurgence crushes ceasefire hopes
snippet: Gold fell to $4,456 per ounce on Wednesday, down 0.74%, while silver slid below $75 as renewed fighting between Iran, Israel and Hezbollah wiped out hopes for a lasting ceasefire. Markets are also pricing in a Fed rate hike before year-end after inflation accelerated, driven by high oil prices tied to the Middle East conflict.

headline: TRUMP SIGNS new Section 232 copper and aluminum tariff rules; restructured duties take effect June 8
snippet: President Trump signed a proclamation on June 1-2 adjusting existing Section 232 tariffs on copper, aluminum and steel, effective June 8 through December 31, 2027. Key changes include a 15% tariff on industrial equipment imported from trade-deal countries and an incentive for foreign manufacturers to qualify for reduced 10% duties by sourcing at least 85% of their capital equipment from U.S. steel or aluminum.

headline: DPM METALS HITS 713 METRES at 2.52 g/t AuEq — massive new porphyry system found 1 km from Chelopech mine
snippet: DPM Metals announced a major gold-copper discovery at the Brevene South Porphyry target in Bulgaria, immediately adjacent to its Chelopech operation. Standout hole EX_BRESPO_03 cut 713 metres grading 1.31 g/t gold and 1.16% copper, including a high-grade interval of 398 metres at 1.48 g/t Au and 1.45% Cu from 1,487 metres depth. RBC Capital Markets called the system "potentially very high-grade," and DPM has planned up to 15,000 additional metres of drilling in 2026.

headline: AYA SILVER BONANZA: 2,176 g/t over 8.4m and 5,100 g/t over 2m at Morocco's Zgounder — west zone now open
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) reported bonanza-grade silver drill results at its Zgounder mine in Morocco, including 2,176 g/t Ag over 8.4 metres and 5,100 g/t over 2.0 metres near pit depth. The western fault zone is "open for expansion" and an exploration drift is advancing ahead of planned second-half 2026 drilling. Aya has completed 30.8% of its 30,000-metre 2026 program.

headline: NORTHERN STAR surges 12.4% — strong drilling at Pogo mine and Australian operations beats guidance expectations
snippet: Northern Star Resources (ASX: NST) led the ASX 200 with a 12.4% gain on June 2, closing at a new 52-week high after reporting high-grade gold intercepts from drilling at its Pogo mine in Alaska and multiple Australian projects. Analysts said the results exceeded expectations and reinforced confidence in NST's full-year production guidance, with the company holding one of the strongest balance sheets among Australian gold producers.

headline: Discovery Silver CLOSES Glencore Kidd acquisition, taking control of historic Timmins underground complex
snippet: Discovery Silver Corp. (TSX: DSV) completed its acquisition of Glencore's 100% interest in the Kidd Operations in Timmins, Ontario on June 1, gaining the Kidd Creek Mine, Kidd Metallurgical Site and associated exploration lands. Consideration was $10 million in shares plus assumed environmental and rehabilitation obligations. New SVP Timmins Operations Dawid Myburgh was appointed immediately on close.

headline: JUNE 30 DEADLINE: Trump must decide on 15–30% copper import tariffs — traders pricing in volatility
snippet: By June 30, the Commerce Secretary must deliver an update on U.S. refined copper markets, after which President Trump may impose a 15% tariff starting January 2027 and 30% from 2028 — a separate decision from the Section 232 tweaks already signed this week. Copper has surged 36% year-over-year and Goldman Sachs is targeting $13,735/tonne; the phased tariff threat could widen the CME premium further and distort global supply chains.

headline: GoldSeek: Gold, silver and copper show bullish technical setups entering June — key levels to watch
snippet: GoldSeek's Asian Metals Market Update for June 2 outlines bullish near-term technicals for gold, silver and copper, with precious metals supported by Fed rate-hike fears and ongoing Middle East tensions. The note flags key support and resistance levels for traders positioning ahead of the June 30 copper tariff decision and any ceasefire developments in the Iran-Israel-Hezbollah conflict.

headline: Experts forecast gold in $4,300–$4,725 range for June; silver seen finding floor near $72–$88
snippet: Multiple analysts surveyed by CBS News expect gold to trade between $4,300 and $4,725 in June 2026, with APMEX's Brett Elliott flagging $4,463 as current support and a 0–5% decline as the base case for the month. Silver is expected to find a floor in the $72–$88 range, with one expert projecting a 10–15% pullback as investor selling levels off before the next leg higher.

headline: AI DATA CENTRES reshaping uranium procurement — analysts see $100/lb return as utilities re-enter market
snippet: The rapid buildout of AI hyperscale data centres is emerging as a new structural driver for nuclear power, pushing utilities back into the spot and term uranium markets after years of under-contracting. More than 85% of institutional investors surveyed expect higher uranium prices through 2026, with a $100–$120/lb range cited as the base case and $135/lb possible if mine supply fails to respond. Uranium is currently trading near $86/lb.

headline: $21.6 BILLION in Q1: Mining M&A hits three-year high as gold majors race to replenish depleting reserves
snippet: Mining M&A recorded 121 transactions worth $21.6 billion in Q1 2026, up from $16.1B in Q1 2025 and $13.9B in Q1 2024, according to White & Case data. Gold remained the most-targeted commodity as producers rushed to replenish reserves at near-record prices, while critical mineral supply-chain security is expected to keep deal volumes elevated through the rest of the year.
